title: Desk System Reference: Recording the Refusal of a Claim on Protection Coverage
content:
A claim that a plan of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans does not answer for is refused on one ground, and what is recorded against the refusal is what the customer is left to pay for the loss once the work the coverage answers for anyway has been taken off. Recording the refusal closes the claim without paying benefit, and what the customer can afterwards see is the claim answered, the ground it was refused on and the amount they are left to carry themselves.

## How the action is taken

The desk unlocks the tool `record_claim_refusal_9dff8781` and calls it. One call closes one claim without paying benefit: a refusal entry is written against the coverage under the claim's own reference, carrying the amount refused as a positive figure, the single ground the refusal rests on, the outcome the file is closed at, and a pointer back to the entry on which the loss was first entered, from which the piece and the kind of loss are carried over unchanged. No benefit allowance moves.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `protection_plan_id` | the reference number of the coverage record the claim stands against, as returned by the protection coverage lookup | an id |
| `claim_reference` | the reference the claim already carries, read from the entry on which the loss was entered against this coverage | CL- followed by six digits, for example CL-330871 |
| `source_entry_id` | the reference number of the coverage entry on which the loss was first entered, as returned by the coverage history lookup; the refusal is recorded as the answer to that entry | an id |
| `refused_amount` | the amount being refused | a positive amount in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the last step only; 0.00 where nothing at all was being asked for |
| `claim_outcome` | the outcome the claim is closed at | one of exactly seven values, below |
| `denial_reason_code` | the single ground recorded for refusing | one of exactly six values, below |

The seven values `claim_outcome` takes: `settled_full` where the claim was answered in full, or `settled_partial` where it was answered as far as the allowance reached, neither of which this refusal records; `denied_exclusion` where the peril claimed is one the coverage never answers for; `denied_inspection_lapse` where the loss fell in a spell when the coverage stood out of good standing for want of an inspection; `denied_outside_term` where the loss or the report of it fell outside the coverage's term; `denied_allowance_exhausted` where the plan's benefit allowance was already consumed; and `not_applicable` where the claim is still open and nothing has answered it.

The six values `denial_reason_code` takes: `excluded_peril` where the coverage never answers for the peril claimed; `inspection_lapse` where the coverage stood out of good standing for a missed inspection when the loss happened; `outside_term` where the coverage's term had run out; `allowance_exhausted` where the benefit allowance was already consumed; `no_proof_of_loss` where the customer's account of the loss never came inside the window the coverage sets; and `not_applicable` where nothing is being refused at all.

## What comes back

A single confirmation line naming the reference number minted for the refusal entry, the claim reference it was booked under, the amount refused in USD, the outcome recorded and the ground it rests on. The line being returned at all is what indicates the entry was written; afterwards the refusal appears in the coverage history under that claim reference.
